title: Arrhenius plot of conductivity-temperature product for different compositions
summary: The figure presents Arrhenius-type plots showing the natural logarithm of the product of conductivity and temperature (ln(σT)) as a function of inverse temperature (1000/T) for various compositions, denoted by 'x'. For all compositions, ln(σT) decreases linearly with increasing inverse temperature, characteristic of an activated conduction mechanism. As the 'x' value increases from 0 to 0.30, the values of ln(σT) consistently decrease across the entire temperature range, indicating a reduction in the conductivity-temperature product with increasing 'x'. The approximately parallel nature of the dashed lines suggests that the activation energy for conduction may be similar for different 'x' values, with the primary difference lying in the pre-exponential factor.
